A.explanation: Speed on landing equals launch speed if levels are equal, but direction is downward to the right, so the velocity vector is not the same.

B.explanation: With no air resistance there is no horizontal force, so $a_x = 0$ throughout the flight, which is a constant value.

D.explanation: Only the vertical component of velocity is zero at the top; the horizontal component stays non-zero throughout the flight.

walkthrough: With air resistance ignored, the only force on the ball in flight is its weight acting vertically downwards, with no horizontal force.
From $F = ma$ resolved into components, horizontal acceleration $a_x = 0$ and vertical acceleration $a_y = g$ downwards, about $9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
At the highest point of the dashed path the upward motion stops momentarily so $v_y = 0$, but $v_x$ remains equal to its launch value and $a_y$ is still $g$ downwards.
On landing the speed is the same as at launch for the same height, but the velocity direction has changed from up-and-across to down-and-across, so velocity is not the same.
Only the statement that horizontal acceleration stays constant at zero throughout matches $a_x = 0$ from the force analysis. This is option B.
